title: Article 50 Compliance-in-a-Box for GenAI Apps
one_liner: An SDK and audit pack that adds machine-readable AI-output marking and disclosure to small generative apps before 2 Dec 2026.
customer: Indie and mid-size generative image, audio and video app makers and API resellers selling into the EU. There are thousands of them.
problem: EU AI Act Article 50(2) requires generative systems to mark outputs in a machine-readable format, and systems already on the market must comply by 2 Dec 2026, about nine weeks away. Small vendors cannot afford lawyers and do not know the standards. Fines are material.
solution: A drop-in library or proxy that embeds C2PA manifests, invisible watermarks and metadata for text, audio, image and video outputs, plus a verification endpoint. It generates an audit-ready evidence file, disclosure text for deployers, and tracks code-of-practice updates.
why_now: The deadline is imminent and enforcement risk is real. Most small AI apps have done nothing, and big vendors' tooling covers only their own models.
revenue_model: $199-1,500 per month for app makers, $30K+ enterprise, and paid verification API usage.
non_obvious_insight: The compliance wave hits the long tail that cannot afford counsel. Watermark tech is commoditized, but audit evidence, ongoing updates and a verification endpoint are what buyers pay for.
first_30_days: Ship an SDK for image and audio APIs commonly wrapped by indie apps. Launch a landing page with a countdown, sell 30 subscriptions at $299 per month through indie and EU AI-Act communities, and publish a free checklist.

title: Memory Budget CI for Game Studios
one_liner: CI tooling and fixed-fee audits that enforce RAM and VRAM budgets per target device, because the assumption that hardware gets better each generation just broke.
customer: Mid-size PC and console studios (30-300 staff) shipping in 2027 to Steam Deck, Switch 2 and 8-16GB PCs.
problem: AI data centers are absorbing the RAM supply. Valve's Steam Machine launched at $1,049 against an early target of about $800, Xbox prices rose, and Switch 2 goes to $499.99 on 2026-09-01. The installed base will stay at today's memory ceilings for years, but studios budget memory as a fixed cap and find regressions in late QA.
solution: An Unreal, Unity and Godot CI plugin that builds against device memory profiles, snapshots per-level memory, attributes growth to specific assets and pull requests, and suggests fixes (texture format changes, streaming pool sizes, audio bank downsampling). Sold alongside a 3-week 'memory diet' audit that finds duplicated and unstripped assets.
why_now: Memory vendors now quote a monthly price and a yes-or-no on volume, per a Valve engineer. Console and handheld price hikes in 2026 mean players will not upgrade into new game requirements. Studios are planning holiday 2026-27 lineups now.
revenue_model: $15-40k per audit, $400-2,500 per month per studio for CI, and later a subscription to a device-profile and min-spec benchmark database.
non_obvious_insight: The industry's optimization culture is about frame time. When hardware gets pricier over its life, the cheapest way to grow the addressable market is to shrink footprint, and most footprint is asset-pipeline waste that can be found and fixed automatically.
first_30_days: Publish an analysis of Steam minimum-spec trends versus the Hardware Survey to get inbound. Ship a free open-source memory snapshot diff tool for Unity and Unreal. Offer free audits to 5 studios in exchange for case studies, and convert 2 into paid engagements.

title: Scrap-to-Tab: Supply-House Credit for Trade Scrap
one_liner: A weekly scrap-and-refrigerant buy-back inside independent HVAC, plumbing and electrical supply houses that pays contractors in credit against their supply-house tab.
customer: Independent supply houses (channel, and they benefit from lower receivables) and their solo-to-10-tech contractor accounts. Downstream buyers are scrap mills, refrigerant reclaimers and rare-earth/copper processors.
problem: Small trades are cash-starved: 1 in 5 subs waits 60+ days to be paid, and residential HVAC shipments fell 25-50% in 2025 with equipment prices about 40% above 2020. Techs burn hours hauling old coils and copper to yards, or leave value in the dumpster. Supply houses carry the credit risk on 30-60 day terms.
solution: At the counter: sorted bins, a certified scale and basic grading. Contractors drop copper, brass, aluminum coil, old compressors/motors and recovered refrigerant (handled via a licensed reclaimer). Credit posts to their account, or cash is paid minus a small fee. We settle with the supply house in cash monthly, which cuts its receivables, and sell graded loads. Later add a bounty for magnet-bearing inverter compressors and motors, sold to rare-earth recyclers.
why_now: The HFC phase-down keeps cutting virgin refrigerant, making recovered gas strategic. The Aug 2026 BIS rule shows scrap is now a national-security asset and 'may add materials'. Hyperscalers are pulling rare earths out of waste streams. The HVAC trough is squeezing small-shop cash.
revenue_model: 10-20% spread on scrap; per-pound fee on refrigerant; supply-house sponsorship; rare-earth magnet bounty.
non_obvious_insight: The supply counter is the only place every small trade shows up weekly, it already extends credit, and it is a natural sorting checkpoint. Scrap value paid as tab credit is working capital the supply house wants (lower receivables) and contractors value more than yard cash.
first_30_days: Sign two independent supply houses in one metro. Place a scale and six bins. Buy at about 85% of local yard price for 30 days, then sell to a yard and a reclaimer. Measure pounds per week and receivables reduction, and pitch other houses on days-sales-outstanding improvement.

title: Wearable-Verified PE Credit for ESA Families
one_liner: Turn any kid's fitness tracker into an audit-proof PE transcript line and an ESA service receipt.
customer: Homeschool and microschool families, co-ops and umbrella schools (about $10-15 per student per month). ESA administrators and clearinghouses (compliance contracts). Gyms and studios that want to bill ESA funds.
problem: PE is the least-supported homeschool subject. ESA homeschoolers get a fraction of what private-school kids do (about $2,000 versus $10,474 in Texas) and must spend in a closed vendor marketplace. ESA programs are audit-anxious. Local climbing gyms, swim schools and martial-arts studios cannot clear vendor onboarding. Screen-fatigued parents want real movement documented.
solution: An app plus a $40-60 band, or existing Garmin/Apple/Polar data shared with parent consent. It logs moderate-to-vigorous minutes and coach-attested skill milestones. It converts them into Carnegie-unit PE credit on a transcript issued through a partner accredited umbrella school. It also generates tamper-evident 'service delivered' receipts for ESA reimbursement. A vendor-of-record wrapper handles W-9, insurance and background-check attestations so a local gym can bill ESA funds. Parents control the data and only summaries leave the family account.
why_now: With 31 states opted into the 2027 federal scholarship credit and ESAs expanding, auditors and SGOs will demand evidence that services were actually delivered. Homeschool ESA marketplaces are closed and clunky. Alpha School has normalized heart-rate monitoring of kids, consumer wearables are ubiquitous, and 61% of teachers want less screen time.
revenue_model: $12 per student per month from families or co-ops. $2-5 per verified session or receipt from ESA clearinghouses. A 5-8% vendor-of-record fee on gym and studio ESA billings.
non_obvious_insight: As tens of billions of public scholarship dollars start to flow, the winning tools will be the ones that produce evidence of delivered service as a byproduct. A heart-rate trace is a hard-to-fake delivery receipt, and PE is the one subject where wearables give clean proof. Fitness providers' idle daytime hours are the supply, and education compliance is the demand.
first_30_days: In one ESA state (AZ or FL), recruit 8-10 homeschool co-ops and 3-5 climbing, martial-arts or swim studios. Sign an accredited umbrella school to issue the PE credit. Enroll about 100 kids for a semester at $12 a month. Ship a minimal web app that ingests Garmin/Apple Health exports plus coach attestation. Take the pilot data to one ESA clearinghouse.

title: Repair-Rights Compliance Portal in a Box
one_liner: A hosted repair.yourbrand.com that publishes the parts lists, manuals, pricing and order forms that US state and EU repair laws require, plus the rules engine and audit trail behind it.
customer: Compliance, legal and customer-service leads at mid-market consumer-electronics, appliance, e-bike, power-tool and mobility brands ($30M-$1B revenue) selling in Washington, Texas, Oregon and the EU. Retailers are a second segment.
problem: Washington's law took effect 1 Jan 2026, Texas applies from Sep 2026 to electronics over $50, Oregon bans parts pairing, the EU directive's transposition deadline was 31 Jul 2026, and an EU repair platform is due 1 Jan 2028. Each regime differs in scope, dates and price rules, and the briefing found nobody selling compliance tooling for repair-information forms or parts-availability tracking.
solution: Portal templates and connectors: product-catalog import, SKU mapping to state or EU scope and effective dates, auto-published manuals and parts lists, a parts order form with a fair-price check, pairing-policy disclosures, an SLA timer and request log for regulators, and an EU repair-information-form generator. Regulatory updates ship as configuration changes.
why_now: Multiple obligations hit in the past nine months (Washington Jan 2026, EU transposition Jul 2026, Texas Sep 2026) and Oregon dates are still unclear in public sources, so brands cannot rely on a single law-firm memo.
revenue_model: $15-60k/year per brand by SKU count, $10-30k implementation, and a per-order fee on parts sales.
non_obvious_insight: The core burden of repair law is publication and response time, which is CMS and workflow work, not legal analysis. Law firms bill hourly for what is really a web app, and the portal also cuts support costs.
first_30_days: Pick 30 mid-market brands with Texas exposure from product listings and email compliance leads a free one-page 'Texas gap audit'. Build a minimal portal for three design partners at a $5k pilot fee.

title: Paid Farm Residencies That Recruit Successors
one_liner: Multi-week hospitality-designed farm stays that let heir-less owners audition would-be farmers, monetising the stay and taking a success fee if a lease-to-own follows.
customer: Owners aged 65+ of orchards, vineyards, dairies and livestock farms with no heir, plus career-changing or remote-working would-be farmers with capital who pay for the residency. Farm Credit lenders and estate lawyers are referral partners.
problem: About one-third of US farmers have no obvious heir, and only about 1 in 4 has a formal succession plan. Over 60% of farmland may change hands in 10-15 years, much of it through estates that listing sites never see. Existing matching programs are listing databases, so skill and personal fit stay unresolved until people actually work together, and farm incomes are squeezed by input costs.
solution: Run 2-4 week residencies at $3K-$6K per guest with lodging, meals, remote-work setup (Starlink and a desk), and structured farm-management workshops on finances, equipment and land tenure. A shortlisted guest can take a paid trial season as a W-2 employee. Provide lender introductions (beginning-farmer loans) and lease-to-own and Buy-Protect-Sell templates, and take a success fee at transition. Winter orchard and vineyard pruning gives a bookable season within six months.
why_now: Remote work and nomad visas created the first cohort able to relocate to a farm without quitting a job. Bankruptcies up 19% and a fourth straight year of row-crop losses are pushing owners to plan exits, and the 'invisible transfer' wave means estates, not listings, decide who gets land. AI-assistant booking now lets tiny hosts sell stays directly.
revenue_model: Guest fees of $3K-$6K. A $750 farmer onboarding fee. A success fee of $15K-$25K or 1-2% of land or lease value at transition.
non_obvious_insight: Successors are not found in databases but in the third week of living together, so hospitality is the screening technology. The stay revenue pays the retiring farmer to audition candidates instead of paying a broker, and the trust built also unlocks the seller-financing that beginning farmers usually lack.
first_30_days: Recruit 6 specialty farms with owners aged 65+ in the Hudson Valley, Vermont, the Willamette Valley and Michigan. Open applications through career-change and nomad newsletters, and pre-sell 20 winter-pruning residencies for Dec-Mar.

title: Parcel-Level Rebuttals to Wildfire Insurance Scores
one_liner: Evidence packs showing a coarse satellite-derived wildfire score is wrong about one specific lot, filed under new statutory appeal rights.
customer: Independent insurance agents and HOAs or fire-safe councils in Colorado and California whose clients face nonrenewal or surcharges. Insurers' appeal desks are a later buyer.
problem: Colorado HB25-1182 (in force since July 1, 2026) makes insurers disclose the parcel's score, credit documented mitigation and offer an appeal. California AB 75, operative July 1, 2026, gives notice and dispute rights over aerial-imagery nonrenewals. But 'owners still have to prove their case', and many wildfire models lean on roughly 30 m fuel layers and stale imagery that misclassify irrigated, gravel-scaped or recently cleared lots.
solution: For each parcel, pull the disclosed model inputs (fuel class, vegetation density, distance to wildland) and overlay multi-date 15-50 cm satellite imagery showing vegetation change, roof material and clearance, plus dated homeowner photos. Produce a regulator-format rebuttal pack with a ranked list of cheap fixes, and give agents a dashboard that scans their whole book for likely score errors. The real edge is a growing database of which input errors insurers concede.
why_now: Both disclosure-and-appeal regimes went live in July 2026 and insurers' appeal desks are unprepared. Commercial constellations, including 30 cm Pelican and Vantor archives, plus 15 cm HD, have made high-resolution archives cheap. Regulators in CT, NH and PA say imagery alone is insufficient, and NY has a pending bill.
revenue_model: $149-$299 per parcel via agents. $10-$25 per parcel per year for HOA book scans. About $60 per appeal from insurers for standardised evidence intake.
non_obvious_insight: Wildfire scores are averages of coarse layers, so the cheapest way to change a score is often to fix an input error rather than harden the house. The resolution gap between 30 m models and 30 cm imagery is systematic, so a win on one lot tends to generalise to its neighbours and compounds into a book-level lever for agents.
first_30_days: Pick the Colorado Front Range. Recruit 5 independent agencies with 200+ WUI clients each, plus 2 HOAs. Run the first 50 score disclosures at a $99 pilot price per file, and track appeal success rate as the marketing asset.

title: Hardening Passport: Proof That Earns Premium Credits
one_liner: A contractor-paid evidence layer that turns every roof, vent and 5-ft-zone job into an insurer-acceptable credit claim or parcel-score appeal.
customer: Roofing, vent-retrofit and defensible-space contractors (5-50 crews) in Colorado and California, paying per verified job. Homeowners get the packet bundled with the work.
problem: Insiders assume mitigation credits fail because insurers do not want to give them. Colorado HB25-1182 (in force July 1 2026) now forces disclosure of the parcel score, credit for documented mitigation and an appeal. But homeowners cannot produce insurer-grade proof. One owner reports 'a thousand bucks' off after a $75,000 metal roof, and Boulder's rebate is capped at $500. Contractors lose sales because the payback cannot be shown.
solution: A phone capture flow for crews: geotagged before/after photos, roof class and vent model certificates, 5-ft clearance measurements, all mapped to IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home criteria and each carrier's credit form. It outputs a ready-to-file credit packet and, in Colorado, an appeal letter citing the disclosed score. Contractors use it as a sales line ('we file your discount').
why_now: HB25-1182 took effect July 1 2026 and California AB 75 became operative the same day. IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home just expanded to Washington. This is the first time a statute gives proof a place to land.
revenue_model: $49-99 per verified job or $199/month per crew. Later, carriers pay per accepted credit, and verified-hardening portfolio data is sold to carriers and reinsurers.
non_obvious_insight: Scoring is commoditizing (MSCI paid only $120M cash for First Street), but neutral proof is still scarce. Insurers cannot advocate for the policyholder, so the party with the incentive and the field access is the contractor.
first_30_days: Sign 5 Front Range roofers or mitigation crews. Build the capture flow as a web app around the IBHS checklist. Hand-assemble 50 packets, file them with 3 carriers, and track the acceptance rate as the core proof metric.

title: Flood Closing Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A day-one flood file on every purchase: elevation, zone challenge, private flood substitute and NFIP-lapse fallback.
customer: Title and escrow agencies and mortgage brokers in coastal and riverine markets, with contingency fees from homeowners.
problem: NFIP authority expires Sept 30 2026 after more than 30 short-term extensions. In the 2010 lapse about 1,400 closings a day were delayed or cancelled (secondary source). Even without a lapse, zone and elevation problems surface on day 25 of a 30-day contract, and premiums must roughly double toward full risk.
solution: An order-time 'Flood File': LiDAR-derived elevation, zone confirmation, candidates for a Letter of Map Amendment, an instant private-flood quote with a compliance letter as an NFIP substitute during lapses, and a Risk Rating 2.0 estimate. Title agencies embed it in their order flow.
why_now: Authority lapses in two days, and premium glide-path increases make every flood file a live cost.
revenue_model: $95-250 per file, $500-1,500 contingency for successful zone removal, and private flood placement commission.
non_obvious_insight: Buyers and lenders pay to avoid closing delays. Zone challenges are an arbitrage, since a successful removal saves the owner premiums every year.
first_30_days: Contract with 5 title offices, partner with a surveyor, hand-deliver 100 files, and track removal success rates.

title: Sovereign Data Vaults in Orbit
one_liner: Encrypted national-records backups stored in orbit, out of reach of seizure, cyber-wipe or flood.
customer: Governments of small, exposed or at-risk states (Baltics, Pacific island nations, Ukraine, Taiwan-type buyers), central banks and national archives.
problem: Countries already run 'data embassies' in friendly data centers, but those still sit on someone's soil. A wipe, seizure, war or sea-level loss can strand civil registries, land titles and treasury records.
solution: Start with a hosted-payload vault on a partner satellite: an append-only, radiation-tolerant encrypted store holding registries and legal records, with keys held by the customer under multi-party control and a dead-man retrieval process. Grow into dedicated vault satellites.
why_now: Rideshare pricing makes small payloads cheap. 2025 demonstrations of storage and compute in orbit (Lonestar's data payloads, Starcloud's reported H100 launch) showed the concept works. Geopolitical risk to state data has risen.
revenue_model: Feasibility studies $50-150k. Multi-year vault contracts of $1-5M per year. Per-TB-year storage fees after launch.
non_obvious_insight: Governments already pay for offshore backups. The extraterritorial jurisdiction of orbit can be sold as a legal and physical guarantee, not as a gadget.
first_30_days: Approach digital-government offices in Estonia, Tuvalu, Ukraine and Taiwan-type buyers with a paid feasibility study. Line up a hosted-payload slot with an existing operator. Design the key-custody model with a legal adviser on treaty and jurisdiction questions.

title: Stablecoin Depeg and Freeze Cover
one_liner: GENIUS made stablecoins legal, not insured. Sell corporate treasurers parametric cover for issuer depeg, redemption suspension and wallet freezes so their risk committees will approve holding balances.
customer: Treasurers and CFOs at mid-market and payments companies holding $1M-$100M in USDC or USDT, including corporate clients of the new Citi and Coinbase flow.
problem: GENIUS gives holders priority claims but no deposit insurance. USDT is about $140B and USDC about $74B, the Senate Democrats' Tether report alleges $2B of Iranian flows against $550M frozen, and Bitcoin has drawn down about 50%. Auditors and risk committees want risk transfer, and there is none.
solution: Parametric cover that pays when a named stablecoin trades below a threshold (for example $0.985) for 72 hours on defined venues, when redemption is suspended beyond a set number of days, or when the issuer freezes the insured's wallets. Price from on-chain and reserve-attestation data and place capital with crypto-native and traditional ILS providers through an MGA.
why_now: Corporate flows went live on 2026-09-28. The Fed proposed reserve and capital rules on 2026-09-24, making issuer risk legible. Annual volume is over $90T, and softening reinsurance gives capital a reason to look at new risks.
revenue_model: Premium of about 0.3-1.0% of covered balance per year, MGA commission, and a paid reserve-monitoring and rating subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume regulated equals safe, but corporate risk committees need transferred risk, not comfort. The trigger is objective and cheap to verify, and an independent reserve monitor and rating is a valuable by-product.
first_30_days: Publish a public reserve and peg-monitoring dashboard as a lead magnet and pitch 20 treasurers. Negotiate a first $10M of quota-share capacity from a crypto-native capital provider and pilot with a payments company holding customer float.

title: Incretin-in-a-Drop Assay for Life Underwriting
one_liner: A dried-blood-spot or oral-fluid lab test that tells insurers whether an applicant is actually on semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron or retatrutide.
customer: Life and disability insurers, reinsurers, MGAs and paramedical exam vendors, with bariatric programs, trial sponsors and outcome-based employer programs as follow-on buyers.
problem: Cash-pay and direct-ship fills (LillyDirect, NovoCare, telehealth-partner pharmacies, compounders, gray market) are only partly visible in claims-based Rx histories, so BMI looks 'preferred' while drug-supported. Stopping the drug means rebound and adverse selection. Gray-market retatrutide is invisible by design.
solution: A validated LC-MS/MS panel (semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron, cagrilintide, retatrutide) run by a partner CLIA lab as an add-on to the paramedical exam, returning 'on-board, recent use or none'. Later expansions to pre-op verification, adherence-verified outcome contracts and a consumer 'proof of adherence' report.
why_now: Published LC-MS/MS methods for semaglutide and tirzepatide matured in 2026, the FDA's LDT rule was vacated in 2025, and cash-pay pill volume exploded in 2026 (Wegovy pill >2M scripts).
revenue_model: $25-45 per test as an underwriting add-on, volume tiers for carriers, and later $79 consumer or clinician tests.
non_obvious_insight: This is the first mass-market chronic drug that bypasses the industry's data plumbing. Underwriters will pay for direct measurement over questionnaires because the cost of a wrong mortality class is far above $35.
first_30_days: Ask two Rx-history vendors what share of DTC fills they see. Contract a CLIA tox lab to validate an assay from published methods. Pitch 10 MGAs and reinsurer innovation teams, and run a paid 200-sample blinded pilot with one friendly insurer, with consent and state unfair-discrimination rules reviewed by counsel.

title: Referee Pathway: Officiating as a School Credential
one_liner: A semester-long, credit-bearing officiating course that puts teens in mentored cohorts on paid youth games, fixing the referee shortage by fixing retention.
customer: District CTE directors and state high-school athletic associations are the buyers. Youth leagues and game assignors are paying placement partners. Students (14+ where state rules allow) are the beneficiaries.
problem: Youth and high-school games are shortened or cancelled for lack of officials. Widely cited surveys say most new officials quit within two years, largely because of abuse from parents and fans. Meanwhile teens lack decent first jobs, entry-level white-collar hiring has cracked, and districts are chasing CTE pathways that lead to real work.
solution: A CTE elective, 'Officiating and Conflict Management'. Students learn rules, mechanics, film review and de-escalation role-play. They then work mentored, paid assignments as a cohort (never alone) at rec-league games, with body-worn cameras or comms for protection. The output is a portable 'Registered Official' credential aligned with the state association's licensing. We sell curriculum, assignment scheduling and an insurance wrapper.
why_now: The officials shortage has persisted since COVID and many states have passed laws penalizing assault on officials. CTE enrollment is rising (vocational-heavy public two-years grew 11.7% in Spring 2025). After the entry-level AI job shock, schools and parents want credentials tied to human judgment. Sports is one of the few settings where judgment under pressure is the actual job.
revenue_model: $150-300 per student license paid by districts from CTE budgets. An 8-10% platform fee on paid assignments (typically $40-80 per game). State-association sponsorships and body-cam/insurance partner rebates. A 40-student district cohort is roughly $8-12k plus assignment fees.
non_obvious_insight: The shortage is a retention problem caused by isolation and abuse in an official's first 20 games, not a recruiting problem. A school cohort is the only structure that gives new officials a team, a mentor and institutional backing. De-escalating under hostile scrutiny is also a transferable credential for security, hospitality, HR and healthcare jobs.
first_30_days: Pitch 2-3 CTE directors and the local officials' association. Run a 10-12 week after-school pilot for 30 students, funded by a rec league or booster at about $99 per student. Track how many are still officiating a season later against the roughly 20% baseline. Use the retention data and a league letter of support to pitch the state association.

title: Common Rooms: Community-Share Buyouts of Neighborhood Bars
one_liner: A studio that helps retiring owners sell beloved bars, cafes, bookstores and cinemas to hundreds of neighbors through community-share offers, then supplies a manager and shared back office.
customer: Owners over 60 of profitable independent third-place businesses who can't find a buyer, plus neighbors who buy $100-500 shares. Commercial landlords are a third stakeholder.
problem: Boomers own most main-street businesses and many will simply close, because a qualified buyer with SBA-loan credit is rare. Communities lose their remaining third places while loneliness is a public-health issue.
solution: The UK community-pub playbook, using US tools: a Reg CF offering (up to $5M a year), an LLC or co-op with member voting, a pre-launch pledge drive to prove 300-800 neighbor investors, a professional general manager, and a shared back office (bookkeeping, permits, POS, purchasing) across all venues in the portfolio. Community shares replace acquisition debt so the business isn't forced to service a loan.
why_now: Peak-65 owners are exiting in volume, Reg CF and its platforms are mature, and retail vacancy plus loneliness make the case politically easy. In the UK, community pubs have raised about GBP 35M from 37,500+ shareholders, but the US has no equivalent operator.
revenue_model: Success fee of 3-5% of the raise, a monthly management-services contract ($1.5-3k) per venue, and vendor rebates from pooled purchasing.
non_obvious_insight: Community ownership doesn't sell returns, it sells guaranteed regulars. 500 shareholders who each show up twice a month are a customer base that exists before the doors reopen, and that is why these businesses survive at much higher rates than buyer-owned ones. The moat is the repeatable legal and marketing kit and the shared back office, not any single deal.
first_30_days: Choose one metro and phone 25 owners over 60. Find three with positive cash flow willing to sell at roughly 2-3x seller's discretionary earnings. Launch a pledge page ('would you put $250 into saving X?') to prove demand, and retain securities counsel for a templated Reg CF filing. Charge a small engagement fee up front, with the balance due on close.

title: Notary for AI Agents' Authority to Sign
one_liner: A registry of signed, scoped, revocable 'mandates' that let a company's AI agents prove to counterparties what they may commit to, with a legal opinion and an insurer behind each.
customer: SMBs and mid-market firms deploying purchasing, AR/AP, sales-ops and scheduling agents (finance and ops leads), the fintech and AP-automation platforms embedding those agents, and the vendors on the receiving end.
problem: Agents now email vendors, accept quotes, change orders and click 'I agree'. Counterparties cannot tell whether an agent had authority, whose it is, or its spend limit, and companies cannot prove afterward what they authorized. Contract-formation doctrine (electronic-agent provisions, apparent authority) predates this. Payment protocols carry payment mandates, not authority to bind.
solution: Phase one: a legal template and JSON mandate schema (principal, agent identity, scope by category and counterparty, dollar cap, expiry, escalation), signed as verifiable credentials, with a public verify API and a revocation registry, an audit log, and a law-firm opinion letter on enforceability for the first US states. Any counterparty agent can call a check_mandate MCP tool. Phase two: an MGA-backed insurance product for agent commitments up to the mandate cap.
why_now: MCP and agent-payment protocols emerged in 2025 and small-firm agent adoption is visible now (60+ firms on MyCase's connector in one month), yet the contract-authority layer between payments and law has no owner (background, verify).
revenue_model: $50-500/month per business, per-verification fees for high-volume counterparties, an insurance premium share, and $10-25k enterprise opinion-letter packages.
non_obvious_insight: Payment rails answer 'can this agent pay?' while the law asks 'was it authorized to bind?', and that depends on documented delegation, the same problem powers of attorney and corporate resolutions solved for humans. Whoever sets the schema counterparties check becomes the standard.
first_30_days: Draft the mandate schema and template with a partner law firm and publish an open spec. Pilot with five procurement or AP-agent startups, ship the verify API, get three design partners to put an authority header in agent emails, and open talks with two MGAs.

title: Conversion X-Ray: Scan and Warrant Hidden Risks
one_liner: A 10-day scan of vacant office buildings (LiDAR, ground-penetrating radar, riser mapping) with an AI cost-risk budget, evolving into a cost-overrun warranty backed by the data.
customer: Buyers of distressed office evaluating conversion, their construction and mezzanine lenders, and later sureties and insurers.
problem: Conversions fail on unknowns: slab thickness and post-tension cables, asbestos and fireproofing, riser locations, window operability, structural transfers. Buyers price with averages and blow budgets by 20-40%, and lenders demand large contingencies or refuse.
solution: A rapid package for 40-300k sf buildings: handheld or drone LiDAR, GPR on slabs, facade thermal imaging, MEP riser mapping and sample testing. An AI cost-risk model outputs a per-unit cost distribution and a P80 budget in 10 days. As actual-versus-predicted data accumulates, offer a warranty or overrun cover.
why_now: $39B of office debt matures within 12 months and the buyer pool needs faster diligence. Handheld SLAM LiDAR and vision models are cheap, and public-land and affordable conversions require cost certainty.
revenue_model: $0.30-0.90 per sf for the scan, later warranty premiums of 1-2% of hard cost or lender-paid programs.
non_obvious_insight: Every conversion overrun is a data point that nobody collects. The first firm to log predicted-versus-actual cost across 50 conversions owns the only actuarial dataset in a market that insurers cannot yet price, so the scan is the loss leader for an insurance-like margin.
first_30_days: Buy a handheld LiDAR and rent a GPR unit. Scan three buildings at a discount for buyers in bid periods. Publish 'the top 10 hidden conversion killers' and sign two paid scans at about $15K each.

title: NFC Open-Item Tags for Aircraft Shift Handover
one_liner: Tamper-evident NFC red-tags that record every opened panel, disconnected line and removed component on an aircraft, and block sign-off until each is closed with an as-left photo.
customer: Directors of maintenance, quality and safety managers at regional airlines, Part 145 shops, Part 135 fleets and helicopter EMS operators. Line stations with 3-6 techs per shift are the beachhead.
problem: The most dangerous moments in line maintenance are shift change and interruption. A tech opens a panel, disconnects a connector or leaves a cap loose, gets pulled to an AOG, and hands over verbally or with a sticky note. The 'system' is a paper red tag, a whiteboard and memory. The 2024 737 MAX 9 door-plug investigation put undocumented removal of fasteners in front of every director of maintenance. Digital task cards do not fix this, because the physical state of the aircraft between task steps is not captured anywhere.
solution: Tamper-evident NFC tags that hang on the physical thing that is open. A tech taps the tag with a phone (offline-first, because hangars have dead zones), records what, why and who, and hangs it. At handover, the app shows a manifest of open tags by tail. The aircraft cannot be released in the app until every tag is closed with an as-left photo. Export goes to the work order as PDF or CSV on day one, and to the maintenance system through an API later. Techs get a time-stamped record of exactly what they did and left.
why_now: The 2024 door-plug event made undocumented maintenance a board-level topic. The FAA's 2024 SMS final rule expanded safety-management obligations to more operators, and safety departments are looking for concrete evidence-capture tools. NFC-capable phones are standard and cheap tags are commodity, so the hardware cost is pennies. AI is a minor part of this, which is a feature. It ships without data-science risk.
revenue_model: Per-aircraft subscription ($75-150 per tail per month) plus consumable tags at $0.50-1.50 each, the razor-and-blade model that made lockout-tagout a large industrial category. Enterprise tier with maintenance-system integration and safety analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Maintenance software dies at the tech's hands, because anything that adds keystrokes gets skipped. This replaces a paper red tag with something faster, and it gives the tech a personal alibi for their own certificate if something is questioned years later. The buyer is quality and safety, not IT, so it needs no integration with the maintenance system to start. Underneath the software is a consumables business.
first_30_days: Ask your own director of maintenance to pilot it at your line station, so you can test it during real shift changes. Build a progressive web app with offline storage and buy 2,000 off-the-shelf NFC stickers. Run a free 30-day pilot at two line stations and one Part 145 shop, then measure tags closed with photo, handover time and missed items caught. Convert the pilot to $99 per tail per month plus tags, and use the measured near-misses as the sales collateral for safety managers.

title: Neutral Baselines and Neighbor Guarantees for Data Centers
one_liner: A neutral third party installs pre-construction sensors around proposed data centers and administers a developer-funded, automatic payout guarantee to neighbors, so permit fights run on evidence.
customer: Independent and mid-size data center developers seeking 50-500 MW campus approvals in contested counties. County commissions and state regulators are a second buyer because they can make the service a permit condition. Hyperscalers with in-house community teams are not the target.
problem: Permit fights are evidence-poor. Nobody has a pre-construction baseline of well levels, night-time noise, air quality or voltage at homes, so every later complaint about dry wells or a hum can be neither proven nor disproven. Both sides fight on feelings and lawyers. Politics has turned: New York paused environmental permits for data centers of 50 MW or more in July 2026, Texas ordered its environmental regulator to stop issuing new data center permits in September 2026, and local pauses now exist in at least 14 states. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found only 14% of Americans would welcome one nearby.
solution: Baseline-in-a-Box. Over 60-90 days before the application, deploy 30-60 low-cost sensors: property-line night noise, depth and conductivity in volunteer neighbors' wells, PM2.5, night-sky brightness, and voltage sag at homes. Publish a read-only public dashboard. Have a university extension hydrogeologist and an acoustician review the methods. Escrow the data with hash-anchored timestamps so neither side can edit it. Keep monitoring for 10 years. Then add a Neighbor Guarantee: a developer-funded escrow that pays affected households automatically, like parametric crop insurance, when verified well drawdown or noise exceedances occur. No lawsuit is needed.
why_now: In 2026 the moratorium movement jumped from town boards to governors' offices (New York's executive order of July 14, Texas's TCEQ permit halt of September 21). Developers now need social license as much as megawatts, and regulators are actively drafting the frameworks that will say what evidence counts.
revenue_model: The developer pays $75-150k per site for setup, $4-10k per month for monitoring, and an 8-10% administration fee on the guarantee escrow. Counties that write the service into permit conditions create repeat demand. Later, anonymized data licensing to regulators and insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The baseline protects the developer more than the opponents. It is the only defense against future exaggerated or mistaken claims, and it turns 'trust us' into 'audit us'. Parametric payouts replace adversarial claims, which is why a rational developer buys it from a neutral party rather than opposing it.
first_30_days: Pick one county with a pending rezoning hearing (Georgia, Virginia, Indiana, Pennsylvania or Texas). Offer the developer's land agent a free 30-day pilot on 10 neighbor wells with an agricultural-extension partner. Build nodes from off-the-shelf parts at about $1.5-3k each. Present the live dashboard at the public hearing and convert that developer to a paid contract. Use the result as the case study for the next 5 developers.

title: Compliant Format Kit for Card-Break Sellers
one_liner: Counsel-designed formats and software that let breakers, repackers and game stores run randomized break and mystery-pack sales without tripping lottery law.
customer: Independent breakers and repack sellers on Whatnot, eBay and TikTok, plus game stores that run break nights.
problem: Random spot-assignment breaks are being attacked as illegal lotteries under California Penal Code 319. Fifteen arbitration demands were filed in March 2026 for 30+ clients (about 100 expected). A July 2025 suit names Whatnot and Fanatics Live, and a qui tam action was recently unsealed. Independent sellers carry exposure with no counsel and no tooling.
solution: Alternative formats (pick-your-own-team, guaranteed-value floors, no-purchase-necessary entry flows), a per-state rule engine with registration and bonding reminders, an audit-logged randomizer with retained video, age and spend-limit controls, odds-disclosure templates, and dispute-ready records.
why_now: Arbitrations run 12-18 months, so seller uncertainty peaks through 2027. Platforms are defending, not building seller tooling.
revenue_model: $79-299/month SaaS by seller volume, a legal-review add-on, compliance audits, and licensing to platforms.
non_obvious_insight: Litigation targets platforms, but the marginal legal risk sits with small sellers whose margins cannot absorb it. Nobody sells them a compliant product design, and the fix is to change the product (make assignment non-random or value-guaranteed), which software can standardize. Whether breaks are illegal is unsettled, so retain gaming counsel.
first_30_days: Retain consumer-gaming counsel. Publish a free state-by-state cheat sheet. Recruit 20 mid-size breakers through Discords and pilot a pick-your-spot format with a guaranteed floor at $99/month.

title: Closure-as-a-Service for Colleges and Grad Programs
one_liner: Orchestrating orderly teach-outs, transcript custody and student transfers for shutting colleges and graduate programs that the new loan caps and demographics are about to gut.
customer: Small private colleges and graduate programs facing closure or merger, state higher-ed regulators, accreditors, and university systems absorbing programs.
problem: The enrollment cliff plus the end of Grad PLUS and the new caps push small colleges and grad programs (nursing, counseling and others) below viability. Closures are chaotic: teach-out agreements, records custody, transfer-credit mapping, refunds and student communications are improvised, and regulators and accreditors demand teach-out plans.
solution: A standing playbook, software and partner network: pre-negotiated teach-out partners, an AI-assisted transfer-credit mapper across receiving schools, secure transcript and records custody, student communications, and tracking of closure obligations. Sell a 'teach-out readiness audit' and retainer to at-risk institutions before they need it.
why_now: The July 2026 aid reset, K-12 and college demographic cliffs and rising closures make this a recurring workload. State regulators are searching for standard processes.
revenue_model: $20-50k annual readiness retainers, $100-400k per closure project, $5-15 per student per year records custody, and referral fees from receiving institutions.
non_obvious_insight: Institutions treat closure as a one-time catastrophe, but with hundreds at risk it is a recurring, standardizable service, like a bankruptcy trustee, where fees come from the estate and reputation for orderly process determines who gets hired.
first_30_days: Publish a teach-out readiness checklist. Offer a $7.5k readiness audit to 10 small colleges and 2 state regulators. Recruit an ex-registrar and an ex-accreditation consultant as delivery leads.

title: City Micro-Rule API for Group Tour Operators
one_liner: A continuously updated database of group caps, loudspeaker rules, coach drop-off bans, fees and overnight-parking bans across overtouristed places, delivered as an itinerary checker for tour operators and campervan renters.
customer: Small and mid-size group tour operators, DMCs, shore-excursion companies, guide associations and campervan or RV rental firms in Europe.
problem: Cities answer overtourism with many small rules, such as group-size caps and loudspeaker bans in places like Venice and Amsterdam, plus coach access fees and wild-camping bans elsewhere. These live in local-language ordinances, and fines fall on operators and guides. Nobody publishes a single source of truth.
solution: Use multilingual LLM ingestion of municipal ordinances with human legal review for the top 60 cities. The product is an itinerary checker that flags violations and fees, a weekly change digest, an API for booking systems and a WhatsApp bot for guides.
why_now: Municipal crackdowns keep multiplying (Barcelona, Palma, Venice, Amsterdam, the Balearics, Glasgow's levy from Jan 2027). Long-context LLMs make parsing ordinances in many languages cheap only recently.
revenue_model: USD 79-299 per month per operator, enterprise API licences for cruise lines and campervan renters, and paid city packs.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism policy has fragmented into thousands of tiny local rules. The pain is compliance risk rather than any single rule, and every new rule makes the product more valuable.
first_30_days: Curate rules for 10 cities (for example Venice, Rome, Florence, Amsterdam, Barcelona, Dubrovnik, Lisbon, Athens, Edinburgh and Kyoto) with local guides. Sell 10 operators at USD 99 per month through guide associations, and publish free rules-by-city pages for SEO lead generation.

title: Magnetic Maps for GPS-Denied Drone Navigation
one_liner: A data company that maps low-altitude magnetic anomalies and sells the layers that let cheap drones navigate without GPS.
customer: Drone makers and integrators in Drone Dominance and Navy autonomy programs who need GPS-denied performance, and later defense agencies seeking quantum navigation.
problem: Jamming defeats GPS, and magnetic navigation needs detailed low-altitude field maps. Public datasets are coarse, and hardware teams do not want to become mapping companies. The Navy is asking for quantum navigation and degraded-environment navigation.
solution: Fly survey drones carrying vector magnetometers over test ranges, training areas and border regions, publish tiles through an API, and provide a reference navigation filter that drone makers can integrate. Start with the Gauntlet region and US test ranges.
why_now: Cheap, sensitive magnetometers and onboard compute make magnetic navigation practical for small drones. Fleets of attritable drones can also continuously enrich the map. The Navy calls for quantum and degraded-network navigation (verify map resolution claims).
revenue_model: Per-area annual licences ($20-100K per region), per-tile API access, and custom survey work for programs. Defense SBIR funding for range expansion.
non_obvious_insight: The map, not the sensor, is the moat and it compounds. Every drone that flies with a magnetometer improves the map, so the mapping firm becomes the network owner.
first_30_days: Buy two survey rigs and map one test range and one agricultural area. Publish accuracy results. Offer 3 Gauntlet participants a pilot navigation filter and tile access.

title: Audit Desk for Indie Labels' AI-Remix Royalties
one_liner: Independent monitoring, consent management and statement auditing for the royalties that AI covers and remixes will start generating.
customer: Indie labels and publishers with 500-50,000 tracks, including Merlin, A2IM and IMPALA members, and their managers. Later, Merlin itself or collecting societies.
problem: Spotify and UMG will sell fan AI covers and remixes as a paid Premium add-on with 'consent, credit, compensation,' but no attribution method has been disclosed. Merlin joined on Aug 4, and Deezer's remix feature needs artist consent (Jun 24). Indie rights-holders will soon receive statement lines for derivative uses they cannot verify, across several programs with different opt-in rules.
solution: A dashboard that normalizes consent and pricing terms across programs (Spotify, Deezer, YouTube, licensed generators). An independent detector samples public remix and cover outputs using stem-level audio similarity to estimate each catalog's derivative usage. It reconciles the estimate against reported statements and prepares audit-rights letters when the numbers do not match. Delivered as a monthly report plus software.
why_now: The first major licensed-derivative programs launched in 2026, and Suno's Sep 9 move to a licensed-trained model shows a pay-for-use market forming. Indies have the least data and the weakest audit position.
revenue_model: $500-2,000/month per label, plus a contingency of 10-15% on recovered underpayments, which is standard for royalty audits, and an enterprise deal with an indie body.
non_obvious_insight: When a new royalty stream launches without a disclosed attribution method, the party with the least data needs an independent auditor. Royalty auditing is an established, profitable profession that no one has built for AI derivatives yet.
first_30_days: Take 10 indie labels through Merlin and A2IM contacts. Produce a free 'Derivative Exposure Report' scanning YouTube, TikTok and Deezer previews for AI covers of each label's top 50 tracks. Sell the monthly monitor, and recruit an advisor from a royalty-audit firm.

title: Diaspora-Financed Home Batteries for Family Back Home
one_liner: Sell home battery and solar systems to migrants in the US, UK, Canada and EU as a monthly subscription that keeps the lights on for their relatives, underwritten on the sender's credit rather than the recipient's.
customer: Diaspora professionals (Nigerian, Ghanaian, Kenyan, Filipino, Nepali, Bangladeshi) who already fund fuel, diesel and generator repairs for relatives, with installers in the origin city as fulfilment partners.
problem: Families in Lagos, Accra, Nairobi or Manila face daily outages and spend remittance money on diesel and petrol for generators. Local households are unbankable for asset finance, USD lenders carry FX and default risk, and pay-as-you-go schemes collect tiny local-currency payments. The Hormuz shock has raised fuel costs and put about $50bn of Gulf remittances at risk.
solution: A subscription sold in USD, GBP or CAD. A vetted local installer fits a 5 kWh LFP battery plus hybrid inverter (and optional panels) at the relative's home, the sender pays by card over 24-36 months, and ownership transfers at the end. Underwriting uses the sender's developed-market credit profile. A shared app shows the sender live uptime and savings, and the family gets a simple power ledger. On default, the fallback is remote throttling or redeployment of the unit.
why_now: Stationary battery prices fell 45% in a year and Africa already imports more battery dollars than panels. Felix shows migrant payments can run over chat apps at $8B scale. The US 1% tax on cash-funded remittances pushes senders toward card-funded rails (buying goods and services delivered abroad is not a remittance transfer, subject to legal review), and Nigeria and Kenya are opening rules for digital-dollar settlement.
revenue_model: Hardware margin of 15-25% plus a financing spread (about 18-25% effective APR), installer referral fees, and insurance and extended-warranty attach. Dollar collections match dollar-denominated hardware and DFI debt, removing the FX mismatch.
non_obvious_insight: Credit risk is being priced on the wrong person. The one who effectively pays for the outage today is the diaspora sender, through diesel money, and that person has a credit file, a card and hard-currency income. The caregiving motive should also produce lower churn than pay-as-you-go.
first_30_days: Put up a landing page taking $500 refundable deposits through 3-5 Nigerian, Ghanaian or Kenyan diaspora WhatsApp, church and alumni groups. Contract one Lagos or Nairobi installer and ship 20 systems. Use uptime screenshots and family videos for the referral flywheel, and fund working capital from deposits plus a small angel or DFI debt line.
